title: Meeting Ellington at the Cotton Club and the Bobby Hackett Decca album
summary: He recalls meeting Ellington and recording a Decca album with Bobby Hackett in the Glen Gray band.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: I went up to the Cotton Club, rehearsed -- Mills was there. He had given me the two tunes to do. And I really didn't know Ellington. It was the first I had met him. But we got along very -- right away, you know, we got along very well. I think he mentions it in someplace, in an album that came out. I think the album -- it's on the cover of the album that came out that I did with Bobby Hackett for Decca. He mentions something about, you know, mentions my name.
Who does?
Ellington.
Oh, he's quoted on the album?
No, he's not quoted.
(Interruption)
This was Bobby Hackett, an album you did with Bobby Hackett on Decca?
Yeah. Now, that was when Bobby was with the Casa Loma, which -- that's the second time I was with him. They were called down, the Glen Gray orchestra.
And how did Ellington come to make a
Well, now, that was made for Decca, but it was put out by that company, which was not defunct, but it wasn't -- Brunswick. Brunswick put out a sort of a --
Oh, was it a, like a 78 album, about three 78s in it or four 78s, whatever?
Well, no, ours had, I think, six of them.
Six?
Yeah. So we did it in two sessions. I had some wonderful guys there.
What year was this?
It was when I was with the Glen Gray band.
With the Glen Gray orchestra,
This was the second time now.
Yeah, so what year was that? That was in the '40s?
In the '40s sometime, yeah, around the early '40s.
And Hackett was featured?
